title: Graphing a Left-Shifted Inverse-Square Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = 1 / (x + 1)^2 by identifying its parent function, shift, asymptotes, domain, range, and intercepts.

steps.title: Identify the Parent Function and Horizontal Shift
steps.explanation: Replacing x with x + 1 in the parent function y = 1/x^2 shifts the graph 1 unit to the left.
steps.why: Replacing x with x + 1 translates the graph horizontally by h = -1.

steps.title: Determine the Asymptotes, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The vertical asymptote moves from x = 0 to x = -1, while the horizontal asymptote remains y = 0 and the range remains (0, infinity).
steps.why: The denominator (x + 1)^2 vanishes at x = -1 and is strictly positive everywhere else.

steps.title: Locate the y-Intercept and Symmetric Points
steps.explanation: The curve is symmetric about the line x = -1, rising to +infinity on both sides of x = -1 and passing through (-2, 1) and the y-intercept (0, 1).
steps.why: Evaluating at x = 0 gives y = 1, and symmetry across x = -1 gives (-2, 1).
